summary:
### TL;DR
- **No GitHub Actions changes, deprecations, or deadlines today.** The only Actions update is a small docs fix to the [Quickstart](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/get-started/quickstart).
- **Secret scanning detectors now run inside Copilot security review, in public preview.** This covers Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, Copilot SDK integrations, and Copilot code review. It is off by default and consumes AI credits. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-secret-scanning-on-demand-for-developers-and-agents))
- **Copilot code review adds secret detection, Adaptive effort, and cross-repository context** (all public preview). Copilot code review for Azure Repos is now GA. ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-copilot-code-review-adaptive-effort-secret-detection-and-more))
- **Several new models are enabled automatically unless admins opt out:** GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol and MAI Code 2 / MAI Code 2 Flash. ([GPT-6.2](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-openais-gpt-6-2-astra-and-gpt-6-2-sol-now-available), [MAI](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-mai-code-2-and-mai-code-2-flash-in-github-copilot))

### Action required
There are no breaking changes or dated deadlines. Admins may want to review these behavior changes:
- **New models are on by default.**
  - GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, MAI Code 2, and MAI Code 2 Flash are automatically enabled under default model enablement. The exceptions are if an admin has turned off the global default or explicitly disables them.
  - Copilot Business/Enterprise admins who restrict models should check the model policy in Copilot settings.
  - All four models are billed under usage-based billing.
  - ([GPT-6.2](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-openais-gpt-6-2-astra-and-gpt-6-2-sol-now-available), [MAI](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-mai-code-2-and-mai-code-2-flash-in-github-copilot))
- **JetBrains: Claude and Codex are now off under enterprise-managed settings.**
  - In Copilot for JetBrains, enterprise-managed settings disable Claude and Codex unless an administrator policy allows an exception.
  - Teams that rely on these providers in JetBrains may need a policy exception.
  - ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-github-copilot-in-jetbrains-ignite-releases))
- **Copilot CLI Entra sign-in needs a minimum version.** Microsoft Entra sign-in requires Copilot CLI **1.0.113 or later** (run `copilot update`). ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-github-copilot-cli-adds-microsoft-entra-sign-in-as-a-preview))

### Security improvements
- **On-demand secret scanning for developers and agents (public preview)**
  - **What it does:**
    - Copilot's security-review specialist can now run GitHub's secret scanning detectors.
    - These cover 500+ provider patterns from 150+ partners, plus a fine-tuned model for credentials without a recognizable format, such as passwords in connection strings.
    - It checks changes only, not repository history.
  - **How to enable it:** Secret scanning is **off by default**. Per tool:
    - **Copilot CLI:** `/settings aiSecretDetection on`
    - **Copilot app:** Settings > Experimental > AI secret detection
    - **Copilot SDK:** set the `SECURITY_REVIEW_FINE_TUNED_MODEL` flag
    - **Copilot code review:** Settings > Copilot > Code review > Secret scanning
  - **Cost:** No additional plan is required. Scans consume AI credits under the Secret Protection AI Credit SKU.
  - ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-secret-scanning-on-demand-for-developers-and-agents))
- **Copilot code review: secret detection (public preview)**
  - It flags exposed credentials in PR review comments before merge, using both deterministic (regex) and LLM-based detection.
  - To enable it, go to repository or organization settings > Copilot > Code review.
  - ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-copilot-code-review-adaptive-effort-secret-detection-and-more))
- **Copilot code review: Adaptive effort (public preview)**
  - Copilot picks Lite, Balanced, or Max per pull request based on its complexity and risk.
  - It never exceeds the maximum effort level set for the enterprise, organization, or repository.
  - Cross-repository context (public preview, public repos only) lets reviews find dependent code in related repositories.
  - ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-copilot-code-review-adaptive-effort-secret-detection-and-more))
- **Copilot CLI: Microsoft Entra sign-in (public preview)**
  - Enterprises using EMU via OIDC get silent SSO to GitHub with their Entra identity.
  - Requirements: a Copilot Business or Enterprise license and the Copilot CLI policy enabled.
  - Supported on Windows and macOS; Linux support will follow.
  - ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-github-copilot-cli-adds-microsoft-entra-sign-in-as-a-preview))
- **JetBrains: Cloud sandbox (public preview)**
  - Copilot sessions can run in an isolated, GitHub-hosted environment instead of on the local machine.
  - ([source](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-17-github-copilot-in-jetbrains-ignite-releases))

### Docs changes worth reading
- **New tutorial: "Secure code from an agent's first commit to production"**
  - A guided journey covering security across the development lifecycle for agent-written code.
  - It starts with a "Review an agent's changes before you push" track: local security review and secret scanning from Copilot CLI, your IDE, or the Copilot app.
  - ([doc](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/tutorials/secure-code-from-commit-to-production), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/5baaf9699698ed5f935ebc84ea2693a88ab6d8f7))
- **Actions Quickstart fix**
  - The job sidebar heading now reads **All jobs** instead of **Jobs**, matching the current UI. The outdated screenshot was removed.
  - ([doc](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/get-started/quickstart), [commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/841308525efb1a0f005369d83c54183068bb65d2))
- **Other code-security doc edits** (AI Scan, Autofix, push protection, AI push protection, risk assessment) only add category tags or update a CTA link. There is no substantive content change. ([commit](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/5baaf9699698ed5f935ebc84ea2693a88ab6d8f7))

changelog.title: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol now available
changelog.text: OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are now generally available in GitHub Copilot. Both models are designed for agentic coding and code review, with stronger coding judgment than earlier GPT-6 models. In early testing, both caught significantly more real issues in code review than earlier GPT-6 models while using fewer tokens. GPT-6.2 Astra: OpenAI’s latest Astra model for agentic coding and terminal work. In early testing, it caught significantly more issues in code review than GPT-6 Astra and completed agentic coding tasks using noticeably fewer tokens. GPT-6.2 Sol: OpenAI’s latest Sol model for complex agentic coding and in-depth code review. In early testing, it caught nearly twice as many real issues in code review as GPT-6.1 Sol while keeping its findings accurate. These models are billed at provider list pricing under usage-based billing. See Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot for details. Availability in GitHub Copilot GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol are available to Copilot Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise users. You can select the models in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot coding agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile on iOS and Android JetBrains IDEs Xcode Eclipse Rollout will be gradual. Check back soon if you don’t see the models yet. Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to GPT-6.2 models through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are automatically enabled unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables these models. Learn more To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback. The post OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol now available appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Copilot code review: Adaptive effort, secret detection, and more
changelog.text: GitHub Copilot code review now helps you catch more issues earlier, with less effort. Adaptive matches review depth to each pull request, so routine changes get a quick pass and risky changes get a deeper look. Reviews can also draw on related repositories and flag exposed secrets before they reach your main branch. Features in public preview are subject to change. Adaptive, cross-repository context, and secret detection are available to Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans. 🎯 Adaptive: The right review effort for each pull request Today, someone has to decide in settings or when requesting a review, what review effort level each pull request needs. A documentation update may only need Lite , while a change to authentication logic benefits from Max . Adaptive makes that choice for you. Copilot looks at each pull request’s complexity and risk, then reviews it with Lite , Balanced , or Max . Each review shows which effort level Adaptive picked. Adaptive is now in public preview. ⚙️ Configure Adaptive You can select Adaptive for a single pull request from the “Reviewers” bar, or set it as your default review effort in personal, repository, organization, or enterprise settings. Balanced remains the default review effort level. Adaptive never picks a level above the maximum review effort level set for your enterprise, organization, or repository. To learn more, see Configuring code review by GitHub Copilot . ⚠️ The maximum review effort level configured in Copilot code review settings determines which levels Adaptive can choose from. 🔗 Cross-repository context Changes often affect code outside the repository you’re working in. With cross-repository context, Copilot code review can read related public repositories during a review, so it can find code in other repositories that depends on your change. It can also find relevant context from documentation stored in other repositories, custom instructions and skills, and more. Cross-repository context is now in public preview for public repositories. 🔐 Secret detection in reviews Copilot code review can now flag exposed secrets in your pull requests. Using both deterministic and non-deterministic approaches, Copilot code review points out exposed credentials in review comments, so you can remove them before you merge. Secret detection in Copilot code review is now in public preview. Secret detection is supported for the following types: Known formats. GitHub collaborates with 150+ technical partners through GitHub’s secret scanning partnership program in order to build out high-confidence secret detectors. These 500+ secret types use deterministic methods like regex to find secrets. AI/ML-detected secrets. Copilot code review also detects secrets without recognizable format. It uses LLMs and GitHub’s purpose-built model for secret to find exposed secrets. To turn on secret detection, go to your repository or organization settings and select Copilot , then Code review . To learn more, see Secret scanning . 📊 Track review outcomes by repository You can now see how Copilot code review feedback is addressed and utilized in each repository. To get started, navigate to the Insights tab of any repository you have read access to, then click Repository insights . For details, see Track Copilot code review outcomes by repository with Repo Insights . ☁️ Copilot code review for Azure DevOps Copilot code review for Azure Repos, previously in public preview, is now generally available. Teams that host code in Azure DevOps can get Copilot reviews on their pull requests, with comments and suggested changes on the lines that need attention. Flexible setup: Administrators turn on Copilot code review at the organization, project, and repository level. Add a branch policy to request a Copilot review automatically on pull requests that target a branch, or request one manually from the Reviewers list. changelog.title: MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot
changelog.text: The next generation of Microsoft AI (MAI) coding models has arrived in GitHub Copilot. Introducing MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash , two new models that represent a major step forward for the MAI-Code family, expanding from lightweight coding assistance to complex, agentic software engineering. MAI Code 2: A powerful, general purpose coding model built to help developers get from request to result with focused responses, practical code changes, and less unnecessary back and forth. Ideal for complex tasks like deep debugging, multi-file implementation, refactoring, and repository-wide reasoning. MAI Code 2 Flash: A lightweight, cost-efficient coding model optimized for everyday development workflows. Well suited for code explanations, targeted edits, routine fixes, and rapid iteration. Both models are designed for agentic coding workflows, giving developers more flexibility to choose the model that best fits their task. Read the MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash announcement for a deeper look at the model’s vision support, coding performance improvements, and efficiency gains. These models are billed under usage-based billing. For more details, see Models and pricing for GitHub Copilot . Availability in GitHub Copilot MAI Code 2: Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise MAI Code 2 Flash: Copilot Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise Both models are available to eligible GitHub Copilot subscribers on annual plans. You can select the models in the model picker in: Visual Studio Code Visual Studio Copilot CLI GitHub Copilot cloud agent GitHub Copilot app github.com GitHub Mobile iOS and Android JetBrains Xcode Eclipse Enabling access Copilot Enterprise and Copilot Business plan administrators can manage access to MAI models through the model policy in Copilot settings. Under default model enablement, new models are enabled automatically unless an administrator has turned off the global default or explicitly disables the model. Learn more To learn more about the new models, see the MAI Code 2 page . To explore all models available in GitHub Copilot, see our documentation on supported models and get started with Copilot. Share your feedback We’d love to hear about your experience using MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash. Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback and help us continue improving these models. The post MAI Code 2 and MAI Code 2 Flash in GitHub Copilot appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: GitHub Copilot in JetBrains, Ignite releases
changelog.text: This update brings remote access, on-device voice dictation, and browser use controls to GitHub Copilot for JetBrains. Copilot users in JetBrains IDEs also get context usage shortcuts, historical diffs, simpler follow-up controls, and improvements to chat reliability. What’s new Cloud sandbox (public preview) Cloud sandbox runs Copilot sessions in an isolated, GitHub-hosted environment instead of on your computer. Copilot can make code changes and run commands and tests there, freeing local resources and allowing parallel sessions. We’re rolling this out in phases. Remote access (public preview) You can now opt in to remote access to make Copilot chats available in other Copilot clients, such as VS Code and the Copilot app. Discover shared sessions from remotely accessible computers, or reopen remote sessions from history to continue the conversation. We’re rolling this out in phases. Browser use (public preview) Paired with GitHub Copilot in Chrome , Copilot’s built-in browser use plugin can open and navigate web pages, read their content, and interact with links, buttons, and forms to gather information or complete web-based tasks. Enable Browser Use in JetBrains under GitHub Copilot > Chat > Enable Browser Use . On-device voice dictation (public preview) You can now dictate chat messages on supported native plugin packages with Editor Preview enabled. Opt in and download a model to get started. Transcripts stay as editable drafts until you select Send . Split mode remote development GitHub Copilot supports JetBrains split mode remote development, with chat and editor UI running on your local client while Copilot operations run on the remote backend. Make sure you have the GitHub Copilot plugin installed both locally and on the remote backend. User experience enhancements You can manage conversations and find model options with fewer steps: Conversation timing : See timestamps on Copilot agent prompts and responses. Session cleanup : Use Delete beside Archive in session history, and choose whether to skip future single-session deletion confirmations. Model picker : Find Copilot Fusion pinned at the top of Copilot agent model management, where it stays enabled even when you deselect the entire model group. Organization usage : See Copilot Access usage in the quota dialog consistently with other organization plans, including organization help links rather than upgrade or overage actions. Steer and queue : Press Enter to steer a running Copilot agent session, or Ctrl+Enter ( Command+Enter on macOS) to queue a follow-up. Inline chat details : See model names and per-response token details while retaining agent session credit totals. Ask mode response footers now show the selected Fusion tier rather than the underlying model, and the model picker stays open when you turn Copilot Fusion on or off. Worktree names : Use shorter Copilot worktree directory and branch names that retain their timestamps. Quality improvements This update improves chat persistence, startup, and recovery, preserves saved history, and fixes proxy-related loading issues and saved Claude Code paths on Unix. You also get clearer error messages for failed tool calls, working historical session diffs on newer JetBrains IDE EAP builds, and improvements to context search, code formatting, input focus, and MCP sign-in recovery. Changed Onboarding and usage tips The chat onboarding tour is now generally available to eligible users. Chat usage tips are available by default, while your saved tips preference remains unchanged. Enterprise-managed providers and Copilot Fusion Enterprise-managed settings now disable Claude and Codex unless an administrator policy allows an exception. Copilot preserves your saved provider preferences. Copilot Fusion now applies enterprise-managed tier defaults while keeping available tiers selectable and preserving your saved choices. changelog.title: GitHub Copilot CLI adds Microsoft Entra sign-in as a preview
changelog.text: GitHub Copilot CLI now supports Microsoft Entra authentication in public preview. You can sign in with your Microsoft Entra account to silently authenticate to a linked GitHub Enterprise Managed User (EMU) account, use your Microsoft 365 Copilot license, or both, depending on your organization’s entitlements. Microsoft Entra authentication for both EMUs and Microsoft 365 Copilot is currently supported on Windows and macOS. Linux support will follow. Enterprise Managed User support For enterprises using EMUs via OIDC , GitHub Copilot CLI now supports silent SSO using Microsoft Entra authentication. You can access GitHub from GitHub Copilot CLI using your Microsoft Entra identity without a separate GitHub sign-in. You must have an assigned Copilot Business or Copilot Enterprise license, and your organization must enable the Copilot CLI policy. In this scenario, GitHub Copilot CLI uses GitHub inference, and usage is governed by the organization’s GitHub Copilot plan. This SSO experience is currently limited to GitHub Copilot CLI and VS Code and is available only to enterprises using OIDC for EMU. To enable Enterprise Managed Authorization for your enterprise on GitHub Enterprise Cloud, see the Enterprise Managed Authorization documentation . Microsoft 365 Copilot license support If your organization is in Frontier and has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license with usage-based billing, Microsoft Entra authentication lets you access models available through Microsoft Copilot directly from the terminal. In this scenario, GitHub Copilot CLI uses Microsoft 365 inference rather than GitHub inference, and you don’t need a GitHub account. Model access and usage limits are managed through your organization’s Microsoft 365 Copilot settings, not GitHub. You can also use the Work IQ MCP server to give Copilot access to your Microsoft 365 work data as context. For more information, see the Work IQ MCP overview . Get started To take advantage of these capabilities, GitHub Copilot CLI version 1.0.113 or later is required. You can update the CLI by running copilot update in your terminal. Steps for enabling each capability in the CLI are provided in the GitHub Copilot CLI documentation . We’d love to hear about your experience using this new Microsoft Entra support. Join the GitHub Community to share your feedback and help us continue improving the experience. The post GitHub Copilot CLI adds Microsoft Entra sign-in as a preview appeared first on The GitHub Blog .

changelog.title: Secret scanning on demand for developers and agents
changelog.text: Secret scanning should keep pace with the way you build software, whether you write code yourself or work with an AI agent. Copilot’s security review specialist now runs GitHub secret scanning, so developers and agents can catch secrets in code changes before they’re merged. You can use the public preview in Copilot CLI and Copilot app sessions, through Copilot SDK integrations, and in Copilot code review. What’s new Copilot security review already looks for exposed secrets as part of its LLM-based review. Once you opt in, it also runs GitHub’s secret scanning detectors alongside that analysis. Provider patterns: Detect more than 500 secret types from GitHub’s growing catalog, built with 150+ industry partners through the secret scanning partner program . GitHub’s fine-tuned model for secret detection: Not every credential has a recognizable format. The model reads surrounding code to identify likely secrets, including passwords and credentials in connection strings. The review checks your changes for secrets. It doesn’t search repository history. Secret scanning in your workflow Review changes as you work. In Copilot CLI and the Copilot app, ask your coding agent to run the security-review specialist. Use its findings to make fixes and request another review, or run /security-review yourself on your changes or an agent’s work. Build checks into your own agents. With the Copilot SDK, your agent can request a security review before returning its changes, without maintaining separate secret detectors. Catch secrets during pull request review. Copilot code review can flag secrets on added lines, including changes that weren’t checked during development, so authors and reviewers can address them before merge. Enable secret scanning Secret scanning is off by default. Until you opt in, security review uses its existing LLM-based detection only. Enable secret scanning for your tool, then request a review: Tool Enable secret scanning Run a scan Copilot CLI In an interactive session, run /settings aiSecretDetection on . Delegate to security-review through the task tool ( agent_type: "security-review" ), or run /security-review manually. Copilot app In Settings > Experimental , turn on AI secret detection . Delegate to security-review through task , or run /security-review manually. Copilot SDK integrations When you create a session, set the SECURITY_REVIEW_FINE_TUNED_MODEL feature flag to true . Delegate from the session agent, or call session.rpc.tasks.startAgent with agentType: "security-review" . Copilot code review In the repository’s Settings > Copilot > Code review , turn on Secret scanning under Security . Request a review from Copilot on the pull request, or set up automatic reviews. Availability and billing In the tools listed above, if you can use Copilot security review or Copilot code review today, you can use secret scanning. No additional plan is required. Scans consume AI credits under the Secret Protection AI Credit SKU. Learn more and share feedback Learn more about secret scanning and supported secret scanning patterns . For Copilot, see how to run a security review in the app or request a code review . Share your feedback in the community discussion . The post Secret scanning on demand for developers and agents appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
